body: THE GOOD NUMBER: China's challenger to Starbucks reported hyper-growth in stores and revenue and improving unit margins, proof (it seemed) that subsidised growth was turning profitable; stock $17 IPO (May 2019) -> ~$50 (Jan 2020). WHY IT LIED: on 2 Apr 2020 Luckin admitted its COO fabricated ~RMB 2.2 bn ($310 m) of 2019 sales; shares -80% in a day; delisted Jun 2020. The improvement in 'store-level margins' was produced by the fake sales. TELLS: (1) Muddy Waters circulated an anonymous report based on ~11,000 hours of store video showing far fewer items per order than reported, an alt-data refutation of the reported unit economics; (2) chairman and founders had pledged most of their shares for margin loans; (3) follow-on equity and a convertible within months of IPO; (4) related-party history of the founding team. TEST: verify unit economics outside the company (receipts, footfall, app downloads, supplier volumes); treat insider margin loans plus rapid post-IPO capital raising as a governance flag. LESSON: unit-economics improvement is the most persuasive number in a loss-making growth company, so it is also the one worth faking. Contrast Eternal, where order volumes were checkable via restaurant partners and third-party data.

data.good_number: explosive store count and revenue growth after a May-2019 IPO; improving store-level margins
data.test_that_catches_it: independent foot-traffic/receipt data; founder share pledges; capital raises right after IPO
data.why_misleading: COO fabricated ~RMB 2.2 bn of 2019 Q2-Q4 sales; items-per-order inflated

title: Hidden trap: Luckin's store and same-order growth
